sentence_stem: Having been informed of the delay in advance,
correct_completion: the passengers rearranged their plans accordingly.
full_sentence: Having been informed of the delay in advance, the passengers rearranged their plans accordingly.
acceptable_variants: the passengers changed their travel arrangements.
the passengers decided to take a later train.

options.why_wrong: The perfect passive participle clause needs a subject who was informed. A train cannot be informed, so the clause dangles.

options.text: the passengers rearranged their plans accordingly.
the passengers had informed the station already.
options.why_wrong: The passengers are the ones who were informed, not the ones who informed. The passive meaning of the participle is contradicted here.

options.text: they had been waiting on the platform since noon.
options.why_wrong: This describes a past situation, but it does not respond logically to the information that was received in advance.

grammar_focus: Perfect passive participle clauses (having been + past participle) and their agreement with the main clause subject
explanation: The stem uses a perfect passive participle, which shows an action completed before the main action and refers to the main clause subject as the person affected. The completion must therefore be a main clause whose subject is a person who could receive the information. Speakers whose first language has no separate perfect participle may find this structure difficult, so it is worth practising in full sentences.
translation: Завчасно дізнавшись про затримку, пасажири відповідно змінили свої плани.
